metadata.title: Full mcp server list/spec refresh (polling + API)
metadata.author: kevalmahajan

description:
# ✨ Feature / Enhancement PR

## 🔗 Epic / Issue
Phase 1 of #1984  (https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/issues/1984#issuecomment-3734591382)

---

## 🚀 Summary (1-2 sentences)
Added configurable per-gateway polling intervals for tools, resources, and prompts, allowing detailed control over refresh frequency with a global fallback. Also added a new POST /gateways/{id}/tools/refresh API endpoint to manually trigger synchronization and receive granular change counts. Complete tools/spec updation (all relevant fields now updated if changed)

---

## 🛠️ Testing

### 1. Manual Refresh API
Use the new endpoint to trigger an immediate sync. 
Update a tool description in your MCP server, call the API, and verify tools_updated: 1.
Add a new tool in your MCP server, call the API and verfiy tools_added: 1

NOTE: Orchestrate Usecase: For servers with one time authentication enabled, the refresh api supports passthrough headers for authentication and then performs the server sync.

```bash

export CONTEXT_FORGE_TOKEN="your_token_here"

# Refresh tools
curl -X POST "http://localhost:4444/gateways/{gateway_id}/tools/refresh" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CONTEXT_FORGE_TOKEN}"

# Refresh tools, prompts and resources
curl -X POST "http://localhost:4444/gateways/{gateway_id}/tools/refresh?include_resources=true&include_prompts=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CONTEXT_FORGE_TOKEN}"
```

Verify:
Response should look like:
```json
{
  "gatewayId": "bc62c2318f2a4954afd6ae6f726560d2",
  "success": true,
  "error": null,
  "toolsAdded": 2,
  "toolsUpdated": 0,
  "toolsRemoved": 1,
  "resourcesAdded": 0,
  "resourcesUpdated": 0,
  "resourcesRemoved": 0,
  "promptsAdded": 0,
  "promptsUpdated": 0,
  "promptsRemoved": 0,
  "validationErrors": [],
  "durationMs": 75.19576100003178,
  "refreshedAt": "2026-01-12T06:50:36.320920Z"
}
```

---

### 2. Per-Gateway Polling (Auto-Refresh):

Configuration in the .env:
```
AUTO_REFRESH_SERVERS=true
GATEWAY_AUTO_REFRESH_INTERVAL=15
```

GATEWAY_AUTO_REFRESH_INTERVAL is the global default, if you want to configure per gateway interval, while creating/updating a gateway, use `refresh_interval_seconds` to configure gateway specific interval for refresh.

1. Add a mcpserver in the gateway.
2. Modify the MCP server after some time (add a tool/remove a tool/update description or input_schema or any tool configuration)
3. Wait for the set refresh interval, notice that the mcp server is polled, and automatically refreshed with the changes done in the mcp server.


---
## 🧪 Checks

- [x] `make lint` passes
- [x] `make test` passes
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing)

---

## 📓 Notes

Key Changes:

**1. Manual Refresh API (POST /gateways/{id}/tools/refresh):**

- Triggers immediate re-discovery of tools, resources, and prompts.
- Passthrough Headers: Forwards allowed headers (e.g., Auth, Custom IDs) from the API request to the upstream MCP server.
- Error Handling: Returns detailed success/failure status and validation errors in the response (200 OK with success: false payload).
- Concurrency: Uses per-gateway locking to prevent race conditions.

**2. Per-Gateway Polling:**

- Added refresh_interval_seconds to Gateway model (DB + Pydantic).
- Gateways can now have individual refresh schedules (overriding the global default).
- Added last_refresh_at timestamp tracking.

**3. Reliability & Monitoring:**

- Refactored _refresh_gateway_tools_resources_prompts to accurately track changes (added/removed/updated).
- Fixed bug where update counts were not correctly calculated.
- Added database migration (Alembic) for new fields.
- Fixed bug where update counts were not correctly calculated.
- Added database migration (Alembic) for new fields.

**4. Tool Spec Synchronization:** 

- Deeply syncs tool definitions (not just list membership). Updates description, request_type, headers, input_schema, output_schema, jsonpath_filter, and auth/visibility metadata. 
- Stale tools are automatically removed.


```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Health Check Loop] --> B{Gateway Healthy?}
    B -- No --> C[Mark Unreachable]
    C --> D[Skip Refresh]
    B -- Yes --> E{Was Unreachable?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Force Refresh - Recovery]
    E -- No --> G{Interval Elapsed?}
    G -- Yes --> H[Refresh Tools/Resources]
    G -- No --> I[Skip]
    F --> H
    H --> J[Atomic DB Commit]
    J --> K[Invalidate Caches]
```

commits.message:
fix: address review findings for gateway refresh

- Guard resource/prompt deletions with include_resources/include_prompts flags
  to prevent accidental deletion when only tools are refreshed (High severity)
- Remove redundant last_refresh_at update in refresh_gateway_manually that
  ran even on failure - timestamp is now only updated on success inside
  _refresh_gateway_tools_resources_prompts (Medium severity)
- Change refresh_interval_seconds validation from ge=1 to ge=60 to match
  the documented minimum and prevent refresh storms (Low severity)
- Update test to reflect the changed behavior

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
commits.author: Mihai Criveti

commits.message:
fix: _validate_tools now returns validation errors tuple

Changed _validate_tools to return (valid_tools, validation_errors) tuple
instead of just valid_tools. This exposes validation errors to callers,
preparing for future propagation to the GatewayRefreshResponse.

Note: Full propagation of validation_errors to the API response would
require changing signatures of connect_to_sse_server,
connect_to_streamablehttp_server, and _initialize_gateway - deferred
to a follow-up PR to keep this change focused.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
